bullets.title: Hunt for the Wilderpeople
bullets.note: ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Hunt-Wilderpeople-Sam-Neill/dp/B01HE1FTGC/ref=tmm_aiv_swatch_0/ref=dv_web_auth_no_re_sig?_encoding=UTF8&_encoding=UTF8&qid=1603504389&sr=1-1&), [Netflix](https://www.netflix.com/title/80096995), [YouTube Movies](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A7rkPMtXxlw)). This film is both hilarious and gorgeous. _Hunt for the Wilderpeople_ was the first local feature to gross more than $1M NZD in its opening weekend at the New Zealand box office. Written and directed by [Taika Waititi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taika_Waititi) ([@TaikaWaititi](https://twitter.com/TaikaWaititi)), this upbeat comedy was exactly what I needed after a rough week. Check out this [short trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dPaU4Gymt3E), and you’ll see what I mean. Bro, good food for the soul, aye!

bullets.title: The Skin Deep
bullets.note:
([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/c/TheSkinDeep/videos?view=0&sort=p&flow=grid), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/the_skindeep/?hl=en)). “Explore human connection — one conversation at a time.” The Skin Deep delivers on that promise. Consider “[Hard Questions for a Mother to Answer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c7X2lKOpozs)” or, for something lighter, try [“Are First Impressions Spot On?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_sgIH81kj78)” The Skin Deep is an Emmy award-winning creative studio exploring human emotion, intimacy, and connection in the digital age, and if you want to go a step further, check out [their question card decks](https://shop.theskindeep.com/) for friends, couples, long-term couples, families, and more. Hat tip to my lovely girlfriend for introducing me to this gem.**What I’m reading** —  
[**The Psychedelic Election**](https://andrewsullivan.substack.com/p/the-psychedelic-election) by [Andrew Sullivan](https://andrewsullivan.substack.com/) ([@sullydish](https://twitter.com/sullydish)). Greek civilization, a mysterious once-in-a-lifetime ceremony at the Temple of Eleusis, and a cameo by Marcus Aurelius… what’s not to like? This fascinating piece touches on a lot, including how people in D.C. or Oregon can, just possibly, be part of the next Renaissance.
